pr_title: shell: telnet: Update to the new k_work API
pr_body:
Update the shell telnet backend to use the new k_work_delayable API. Additionally, make sure that the delayed worked is actually idle after canceling by using the synchronous API.

Fixes #34100
pr_comments:
> I'm not entirely convinced that this is correct on SMP systems: it looks like the work handler and something else can be inside telnet_send() at the same time from different threads (if another thread invokes write() via the transport API)

@pabigot Thanks for the feedback. Perhaps I misunderstood something here, but my intention for switching to synchronous cancel was to prevent such a situation. My understanding is that telnet_send() can be accessed from the shell thread (via the write() transport API) or from the system workqueue (via the work handler). Won't the  `k_work_cancel_delayable_sync()` call block the shell thread until the work is removed from the queue or the work handler finishes execution, therefore preventing the `telnet_send()` from being executed from both threads at the same time?
